task.name: A run whose knowledge delivery failed outright is counted as a control observation, so the report evaluating the knowledge loop treats a broken mechanism as evidence the mechanism does not help
task.story_text:
## Observed

A run in which prior-run knowledge could not be delivered at all is recorded as a control
observation, so the measurement built to evaluate the knowledge loop counts a broken
delivery as evidence about the loop.

Cohort assignment reads the per-phase context manifest and keys on one fact: whether
`included` is non-empty. A manifest reporting `enabled: true` with `included: []` is
assigned to the control cohort, described in the module as "a genuine control"
(`src/theforge/knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py:13-18`).

Two materially different situations produce that identical manifest. In the first, the
index was read successfully and legitimately offered nothing — a project early in its
history, or a story with no relevant prior work. That is a genuine control: the run was
in a position to receive knowledge and correctly received none. In the second, the
selector could not read its input at all and failed closed
(`src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py:308-326`, returning `INDEX_STATE_MISSING`,
`INDEX_STATE_UNREADABLE`, or `INDEX_STATE_STALE_SCHEMA`). That run was never a candidate
for treatment; nothing about the knowledge loop was exercised, and it carries no
information about whether prior summaries help.

The distinction is available at the moment of assignment and is discarded. The selector
computes `index_state`, and the manifest builder consumes it to write an accurate
operator-facing note — "prior-run knowledge index is missing or was never built"
(`src/theforge/task/prior_run_manifest.py:106-120`). But that outcome reaches the audit
record only as prose inside `note`; no structured field carries it, and the cohort
classifier never reads it. The system therefore knows exactly why the selection was
empty, records it in a human-readable sentence, and then draws a conclusion that ignores
it.

The practical result is a report that cannot fail loudly. With a persistently unreadable
index, every run joins the control cohort, the treatment cohort stays empty, and
`forge knowledge-report` prints `insufficient_data` indefinitely while `forge.yaml` shows
the feature enabled. The reading an operator would take from that — "not enough runs yet,
keep going" — is the opposite of the truth, which is that no run will ever qualify.

## Expected

A measurement assigns a subject to a cohort only when the mechanism under study actually
operated on that subject. Where the mechanism could not be applied for reasons unrelated
to what is being measured, the subject is outside the comparison, not a member of the
group that received nothing — treating a failed delivery as a control conflates "the
treatment had no effect" with "the treatment never happened," and biases the comparison
in the direction of concluding the treatment does not work.

The distinguishing question is whether the subject was in a position to receive the
treatment. A consumer that read its input and found nothing applicable has been
legitimately observed and belongs in the control group; a consumer that could not read
its input has observed nothing at all and belongs in neither group. A project with no
accumulated history yet is the ordinary and correct instance of the first case, and must
continue to be counted as such.

This holds for any condition that prevents delivery, not only the ones enumerated today.
Because new failure modes will be added to the delivery path over time, the safe default
is that an unrecognised or unreported delivery outcome excludes the run from the
comparison rather than silently placing it in a cohort: a run wrongly excluded costs
sample size and is visible as such, whereas a run wrongly included corrupts the result
and is not visible at all.

Where a conclusion depends on a fact the system already determined, that fact reaches the
consumer as data it can act on rather than only as prose a human might read. A cause
recorded in a sentence and nowhere else is not available to the code that draws the
conclusion, however accurately the sentence is worded.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** with `.forge/knowledge/index.yaml` absent, every plan/dev/review
  phase would record `enabled: true, included: []`, and `forge knowledge-report` would
  assign all such runs to `without_prior_summary`, growing a control cohort that can never
  be compared against an empty treatment cohort while reporting `insufficient_data`.
- **Evidence:** `src/theforge/knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py:13-18` documents the rule
  ("Enabled with nothing included is `without_prior_summary` — a genuine control").
  `src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py:308-326` returns an empty entry list paired with
  `INDEX_STATE_MISSING` / `INDEX_STATE_UNREADABLE` / `INDEX_STATE_STALE_SCHEMA` when the
  index cannot be read. `src/theforge/task/prior_run_manifest.py:106-120` branches on those
  states to compose `note`, and the returned manifest dict carries no other field derived
  from them. `grep -rn 'index_state' src/theforge --include='*.py'` shows the only non-test
  consumers are the manifest note builder and the replay harness.
- **Ruled out:** the information being unavailable at assignment time — the selector has
  already computed `index_state` before the manifest is built. Also ruled out: the report
  compensating downstream — `forge knowledge-report` reads cohorts from the classifier and
  has no access to the discarded state.
- **Confirmed cause:** the manifest represents delivery outcome only as unstructured prose
  in `note`, so the cohort classifier has no signal distinguishing an empty-but-successful
  selection from a failed one, and its non-empty-`included` test maps both onto control.
- **Affected code path:** `theforge.task.prior_run_manifest.build_manifest`;
  `theforge.knowledge_effectiveness_signals` cohort assignment;
  `theforge.task.prior_run_selector` where `index_state` is currently terminal.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a run whose prior-run selection was empty because its index
  could not be read is excluded from both the treatment and control cohorts in
  `forge knowledge-report`, while a run whose index was read successfully and yielded no
  applicable summaries remains counted as a control.

## Prior art

Issue #2607 (closed, v0.15.0) made the index-state distinction observable, which is why
`index_state` exists on the selection and why the manifest note names the cause. Its
expected behaviour asked for the distinction to be visible in **operator-visible output**,
and that is where it stopped.

This issue is the next consumer along: the cohort classifier is not operator-visible
output, it is the code that draws the conclusion, and it still cannot see the distinction
because the manifest carries it only as prose. The fix is not to re-derive the state —
#2607 already computes it — but to carry it as data to the point where a cohort is
assigned.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
